plan.title: engine:_ts-build: trailing no-op for go-task <3.52 untaken if/fi

narratives.Description: go-task before 3.52 treats an untaken last if/fi as script exit 1. engine:_ts-build still ends on that fi, so every non-runtime task deft:* fails on a consumer deposit. Add a trailing colon no-op after the outer fi.
narratives.UserStory: As a Directive consumer on Homebrew go-task 3.46.x, I want engine:_ts-build to exit 0 when the deposit is not buildable, so that task deft:* verbs do not fail as if the deposit were broken.
narratives.ImplementationPlan: 1. Edit the tasks/engine.yml _ts-build script so a colon no-op follows the outer fi, with a one-line comment that cites go-task before 3.52 and #3381. 2. Keep the consumer-deposit path from running pnpm or engine-pm-run build, keep the framework-source path building when stale and skipping when warm, then verify with the existing engine tests and task check.
narratives.Overview: Authority is analysis+lock comment 5309667759, not the issue body. Do not change engine:invoke. Do not invert is-buildable-source. Do not raise a hard min go-task version. Do not hunt other last-if scripts.

items.title: Trailing no-op after the outer fi

narrative.Acceptance: Given tasks/engine.yml _ts-build cmds, when the script body is read, a command follows the outer fi. A colon no-op is enough. The comment on that line cites go-task before 3.52.0 and #3381.

items.title: Deposit no-op and source build paths stay

narrative.Acceptance: Given a consumer-deposit tree where is-buildable-source exits 1, when engine:_ts-build runs, it does not run pnpm or engine-pm-run build. Given a stale framework-source tree, it still builds. Given a warm dist, ts-build-fresh still skips. task check passes. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] has a brief note.
